Build conventions for this console and the ISS console, kept here so decisions don't have to be re-litigated each session. Reference only, nothing on this page is a live setting. Sections are shells right now; content gets filled in together over upcoming sessions.
Data Flow & Storage
Standing Rule
All console data should back up to GitHub, not just Log Book notes and Console Improvements. Losing entered data defeats the point of the console. As of 2026-07-30 this is true: every previously local-only STATE key now has GitHub backup coverage via the generic sync engine, see below.
Two Repos, Two Purposes
  • eddb-console-data (public). Shared with both consoles: courses.json, filenametypes.json, urls.json, sessions.json (bundles sessions, imHistory, issLastNames), and budget.json. Pulled automatically on load; pushed only when the person clicks a Push button, no debounce. Fixed 2026-07-31: courses.json used to wholesale-overwrite local on every pull, silently discarding any edit not yet manually pushed (the "Vacant 1/Vacant 2 keeps needing refilled" bug). Now merges by course num, local wins on a real conflict, same policy as every other synced key in this console, remote-only courses get folded in rather than lost. filenametypes.json, urls.json, and sessions.json still wholesale-overwrite on pull as of 2026-07-31, same latent risk exists there too if a local edit isn't pushed before the next load, just not yet reported as a real problem.
  • eddb-notes-archive (private). Internal/sensitive data only, only ever touched from Mike's copy: hot.json, cold.json (Log Book), improvements.json (Console Improvements), sessionstatus.json (Session Status Log), plus one genericsync_<key>.json file per key covered by the generic sync engine below. These use the debounced merge-before-write pattern, pull-then-merge on load, auto-push 3 seconds after any change, and never delete based on what's locally missing.
  • Rule: nothing personnel-sensitive goes in the public repo, ever. If a new feature needs to sync something and it's unclear which repo it belongs in, default to private and ask.
  • A third, narrowly-scoped token exists for GitHub Issues specifically (used by the Requests tab, shared with ISS copies). It cannot read or write courses.json, filenametypes.json, or anything else in the public repo, it only touches Issues.
  • All three GitHub tokens are embedded in plaintext in this file. They must only ever exist in Mike's copy of the console, never in a copy handed to anyone else, including a stripped-down version for ISS use if one is ever built from this file directly.
Exception Worth Knowing
budget.json lives in the public repo despite being financial data. This is deliberate, not a mistake: the BC console pushes it, and the ISS console pulls it and displays real per-course dollar amounts on the Course Material tab, so ISS staff have budget visibility for planning. Don't treat "public repo" as a hard rule against financial data going forward, this is the confirmed exception, but also don't use it as precedent for personnel data without checking first.
Generic Backup Sync (all other data)
Built 2026-07-30 to close the backlog that used to live here. One mechanism instead of a bespoke sync pair per key: every key in GENERIC_SYNC_KEYS gets its own private-repo file (genericsync_<key>.json), pulled and merged on load (awaited before any tab renders, so nothing shows stale data), pushed on a 3s debounce via persist() automatically, no per-call-site changes needed anywhere else in the codebase. A Data Backup status bar sits below the Data subbar on every subtab, with a Sync All Now button for a manual full pass.
Merge strategy is shape-detected at runtime: array of objects with an id field merges by id (local wins per id); plain array unions and dedupes by JSON identity; plain object shallow-merges (local wins per key, remote fills gaps); primitive keeps local if non-empty, else falls back to remote. Nothing is ever silently dropped. Covers: Personnel, Key Roster, Training, Course Material/STAGE, 4713/47121 tracking, BC Slides, Daily Agenda, Requests, Reminders, QA Eval (the item that actually collided in practice), and every dropdown/reference list. notesArchiveCache is deliberately excluded, retired and superseded by hot/cold, not worth backing up.
If a new STATE key is ever added that should be backed up, add it to GENERIC_SYNC_KEYS and it's covered automatically, no new sync function needed.
Note & Template Field Vocabulary
The Fixed List
Defined once in code as NOTE_FIELD_ORDER, 24 fields, this is the actual source of truth, not a separate doc to keep in sync with it:
REF, DATE, TIME, PURPOSE, PEOPLE, COURSE, LOCATION, TAGS, NOTE, FOLLOW-UP, DUE DATE, RECURRENCE, RECUR TYPE, IMPORTANCE, URGENCY, PERSONAL, BUDGET, ASSIGNED BY, ASSIGNED TO, SUSPENSE TYPE, TONY, LISA, STATUS, KEEP HOT
  • ASSIGNED BY / ASSIGNED TO — the pairing every tasking-style note must use. This is what Tasks tab lookups and the Personnel Team tab's open task list actually key off. Any tab that writes its own ad hoc equivalent (like Policy Review's old TASKED BY / TASK FOR, fixed 2026-07-30) makes its notes invisible to both.
  • NOTE — the generic body/description field. Same rule applies: a tab inventing its own field for the note body (Policy Review's old TASK field) won't get picked up wherever code expects NOTE specifically.
  • TONY / LISA — Yes/No flags, not free text, whether this item needs to go in front of Tony or Lisa specifically.
  • IMPORTANCE / URGENCY — Low/Medium/High each, independent of each other, not a single combined priority field.
  • PERSONAL — Yes/No, marks a note as personal rather than work-related (feeds Personal Notes handling).
  • KEEP HOT — Yes/No. Combined with STATUS, this is what decides hot.json vs cold.json placement on save, see Data Flow & Storage above.
  • STATUS — Open / In Progress / Pending / Closed. Closed + Keep Hot = No moves the note to cold.json automatically on save.
The Rule, Stated Plainly
If a new tab needs a tasking field, an assignee field, or a body-text field, use ASSIGNED BY / ASSIGNED TO / NOTE. Don't invent a same-meaning field under a different name, even if it reads more naturally for that one tab. That's the exact mistake that made Policy Review notes invisible to Task Status and the Personnel Team tab until it was caught and fixed 2026-07-30, with a matching one-time migration to repair notes already saved under the old names (see the two migration functions near the top of the script for the pattern to follow if this happens again).
Fields Outside the Fixed List
Parsing is field-name-agnostic: any "FIELDNAME: value" line in a note gets captured and stored, whether or not it's in NOTE_FIELD_ORDER. Several templates legitimately use fields beyond the 24 above, e.g. Leave/TDY notes use START DATE, END DATE, DATE OF ENTRY, NOTIFIED, ABSENCE DUE TO, and some course-tagged notes use COURSE DETAIL or CONTEXT. These are fine and preserved correctly today. One caution for future work: buildNoteMemText (the function that would rebuild a note back into memo-text form) only outputs fields that are in NOTE_FIELD_ORDER, so any of these extra fields would be silently dropped if that function is ever wired up somewhere it isn't currently used. It's unused dead code as of 2026-07-30, so this isn't live, but worth fixing (either extend NOTE_FIELD_ORDER or add a fallback for unlisted fields) before anything calls it.
Date & REF Handling
Date Formatters — five exist, each has one job
  • fmtDate(d) → 2026-07-30. Machine-readable ISO. Use for: storage keys, GitHub commit messages, form default values, anything compared or sorted as a string. This is the only formatter safe to use for equality checks or sorting.
  • fmtLong(d) → Thursday, July 30, 2026. Full narrative date. Use for: the DATE field inside generated notes and Memory Hole templates, anywhere the note needs to read correctly on its own months later without other context.
  • fmtFriendly(d) → Thu, Jul 30. Compact, no year. Use for: UI labels and dropdown option text where space is tight and the year is obvious from context (e.g. "Due: Thu, Jul 30").
  • fmtShortDate(d) → 30 Jul 2026. Compact but includes year, no weekday. Use for: table cells and form fields where the year matters but the day of week doesn't (PPE labels, session date columns).
  • fmtShortDow(d) → Thu, 30 Jul 2026. Same as fmtShortDate plus weekday. Use for: suspense/deadline displays specifically, where knowing it's due on a Thursday actually changes what you do with it.
  • Rule of thumb: if it's read by code or stored as a key, fmtDate. If it's read by a human and the day-of-week matters for planning (deadlines, suspenses), fmtShortDow or fmtLong. Otherwise fmtFriendly or fmtShortDate depending on whether year matters.
REF Numbering — two systems, one namespace
  • nextSharedRef() / commitSharedRef() — a persistent counter (localStorage key eddb_ref_d, floor 1000), used by essentially every note-generating tab (QA Eval, templates, Comms, Budget, etc.) via the sharedRefDisplay field. Reserves a REF the moment it's displayed to the user, before Save; advances only when commitSharedRef runs. This reservation-before-save behavior is deliberate: it lets you generate a draft in one tab, switch to another tab and generate a second note, without the two colliding, even though neither has been saved to the archive yet.
  • nextNoteRef() — scans the actual Log Book archive (hot.json + cold.json) for the highest REF in use and returns max+1. Used only by Memory Hole paste import (when an incoming note has no REF) and the manual New/Edit Note form.
  • Fixed 2026-07-30: nextSharedRef() used to trust its own stored counter blindly. Anything that added notes without going through commitSharedRef (Memory Hole import, manual entry) could push the true archive max ahead of the stored counter without the counter knowing, so the next template-generated note could collide with a REF that already existed. This caused a real collision the same day it was diagnosed (REF 1298, 1303, 1320/1321, 1363 — see Memory Hole consolidation, Session Status Log). Fix: nextSharedRef() now returns whichever is higher, its own stored counter or the archive's true max+1, and heals the stored value when the archive has moved ahead. The reservation behavior for unsaved drafts is unchanged.
  • Fixed 2026-07-31: the self-correction above was only ever as good as local hot.json/cold.json, which never refreshed automatically, only via a manual Pull Latest click on Log Book, or incidentally during an actual push cycle. If a note landed on GitHub from somewhere else (Memory Hole, another device) and Log Book was never opened first, the REF field could look stale on load even though the self-correction logic itself was working correctly. Fix: pullNotesMergeOnLoad() runs once at startup, same additive-only merge policy as the push-side auto-sync (only ever adds a note this browser didn't have, never overwrites or removes anything local), so it's safe to run automatically without asking, unlike a wholesale pull.
  • Between these two fixes, opening the console should now show the correct next REF from the first paint, with no manual pull required.
  • If a collision still happens anyway (e.g. two REFs assigned externally, outside the console entirely), the recovery procedure used during the 2026-07-30 Memory Hole consolidation is the standard: renumber the colliding entry to the next available number rather than overwrite; if two entries turn out to be the same note with different field completeness, merge into the more complete version rather than keep both; drop confirmed duplicates rather than keep a redundant copy; fill placeholder text like [note text] from surrounding context only when the intended content is unambiguous; anything that can't be cleanly resolved gets flagged directly inside the document itself, not just mentioned in chat.
UI Layout Rules
Generate / Save Row
  • Order inside a .genrow: primary action first (Generate, or the section's equivalent like Close Out Task or Reassign Task), then Save to Log Book immediately next to it, then Reset if the section has one, then a status hint span last.
  • Save to Log Book buttons all share one class, .na-savelb-btn, and one global delegated click handler keyed by data-src/data-status. New sections should hook into this shared handler rather than writing a bespoke save function.
  • No auto-save-on-generate, this stays a manual button. Generate is a draft step; auto-saving would create duplicate permanent entries under new REF numbers, pushed to GitHub within seconds, removing the only checkpoint to catch a mistake before it's permanent.
  • Exception, Meeting Notes (2026-07-31): one "Save Meeting Notes" action creates every note for the meeting at once (one per discussion item, plus the summary), rather than a separate Generate-then-Save per note. A meeting is naturally one atomic batch of interdependent notes, not a single note, splitting it into N separate Generate/Save cycles wouldn't add a real checkpoint, just repetition. A confirm() summarizing exactly what will be created (counts of hot/cold/summary) stands in for the usual draft-review step.
Output Block Order
Inside .outputs, Email comes first, Memory Hole Entry always comes last with nothing below it. Confirmed consistent across every generator section (4713 Review, QA Eval, Travel, Tasks, Task Status, and others).
Auto-Drop Empty Template Lines
Standing rule, confirmed by Mike 2026-08-01: if a Memory Hole line reduces to a bare LABEL: after substitution (an unfilled optional field), it should be dropped entirely rather than left dangling. Most hand-written sections already did this with an if(value) conditional-push pattern, but a few (QA Eval's Pre-Eval Tasker/Ready for Evaluation Invite DUE DATE line, Requests' Generate Note PEOPLE line) built the line unconditionally, leaving a visible dangling label when empty. The Template Registry's tplSubstitute applies the drop-the-line behavior everywhere by default, correcting those cases as a byproduct of conversion. This is now a blanket rule, not something to re-flag case by case when the same pattern turns up in a not-yet-converted section.
Table Sort/Filter Persistence
Standing rule as of 2026-07-31: any new sortable/filterable table calls wireDataTable(tableEl, 'someStableKey') with a persistKey, not the bare no-argument call. Without a key, sort and filter state live only in that one function call's closure and vanish the instant the table re-renders, which is exactly what broke QA Eval's Status filter every time a course got updated. The key just needs to be unique and stable per distinct table (existing keys: qaEval, taskStatus, budgetDrillCourse, budgetDrillCategory, courseBudget, f4713, keyRoster, sessionExpand, improvements, sessionStatus, courseData). Persistence is in-memory for the browser session only, not synced to GitHub, since the complaint was about surviving re-renders and tab switches, not surviving a reload.
Multi-Trigger Sections
If a section can produce more than one kind of outcome from the same screen (the Tasks tab's three action panels, QA Eval's per-course actions, 4712-1's Approved/Not Approved), each trigger gets its own Save to Log Book button next to its own Generate action, not one shared button at the bottom trying to cover all of them.
Weekly Slides Routing
Where a note can feed into Weekly Slides (currently just the manual New/Edit Note form), the "Add to Weekly Slides" destination selector sits directly above the Generate/Save row, not below it and not buried in an advanced-options area.
Collapsible Section vs. Subtab
  • Subtab — a distinct, frequently-used feature area with substantial standalone content (Data's Course Data, Key Roster, Templates, Standards, etc). Gets its own subbar button and full show/hide container.
  • Collapsible section (.bulkwrap.collapsed) — secondary or occasional content nested inside a subtab or generator section: Bulk Edit under Course Data, Name Aliases and ISS Last Names under Schedule Import, the QA Eval scheduler, and the five topic areas inside Standards itself. Collapsed by default so it doesn't compete for attention with the primary content of whatever it's nested in.
  • As of 2026-07-30, three-level nesting (a subbar inside a Data subtab, like Standards could have had) is an accepted pattern going forward, not a one-off exception, since builds are already trending toward needing it elsewhere. Standards itself ended up using collapsible sections instead, but the option is open for future features where a real second layer of navigation is warranted.
  • Standing rule as of 2026-07-30: any section that is not a tab's primary purpose should be collapsible by default. Applying this requires identifying what the tab's primary purpose actually is before deciding what counts as secondary, see below. Worked example: Notes Archive's primary purpose is searching/viewing your notes, so Import Notes (an occasional maintenance action, not what the tab is for) became a collapsed section, and Your Notes (the actual search) moved up to sit right after the header row instead of being buried below the New Note form.
Primary Purpose & Category, Required for New Tabs
Before building any new tab or subtab, state its primary purpose in one sentence, and decide which Tab Config category it belongs to (Data > Tab Settings). Don't leave a new tab defaulted to General without checking, that's what every existing tab does today only because Tab Config didn't exist yet when they were built, not because General is the right answer for new ones. Everything in the tab that isn't the primary purpose gets built collapsed per the rule above, using the primary purpose statement as the test for what qualifies.
Worked example, 2026-07-31: Course Material's subbar. Primary purpose of the whole suite is instructional-product tools for building and reviewing course material, so every content tab (Timeline, Lesson Plan, 4713, 4712-1, Learning Objective, and the six builder shells) got Instructional deliberately, not by default. Master Settings got General instead, since it's configuration for the suite, not instructional content itself, same reasoning as why Data's own Dropdowns/Templates default to General.
Exemptions
General Work Notes and Personal Notes are exempt from the Generate/Save row pattern above. Their live-preview design, output updates as you type, Copy/Reset/Save grouped at the bottom, is intentional and stays as-is. Don't "fix" these to match the rest of the console without checking first.
Naming Conventions
LocalStorage Keys
Pattern: STATE key in camelCase, mapped to 'eddb_console_lowercasename_v1'. One known exception: the REF counter uses 'eddb_ref_d', no console segment, no _v1, predates the versioning convention. Leave it as-is, don't rename existing keys just to match the pattern, that breaks anyone's existing localStorage on next load.
Function Names
Verb-first camelCase for anything that does something; noun-first camelCase for simple getters. Observed verb prefixes and what they mean here:
  • render* — rebuilds a DOM section from current STATE (renderDataTable, renderImprovementsTable, renderSessionStatusTable)
  • init* — one-time setup for a tab/feature on startup: wires all its listeners, does the first render (initImprovements, initSessionStatus, initDataSubtabs)
  • wire* — attaches listeners to specific already-existing elements, narrower than init, often reused across features (wireBulkAddToggle, wireCopyButtons, wireDataTable)
  • build* — constructs a text/string output, not a DOM update (buildMemNote, buildNoteMemText, ssBuildHandoffText)
  • fmt* — date/value formatting only, see Date & REF Handling above
  • schedule* / run* — always come as a pair for debounced GitHub auto-push (scheduleAutoPushNotes/runAutoPushNotes, scheduleAutoPushImprovements/runAutoPushImprovements, scheduleAutoPushSessionStatus/runAutoPushSessionStatus). New synced data types should follow this exact pair pattern rather than inventing a new one.
  • parse* — turns raw pasted/uploaded text into structured data (parseFieldBlockToNote, parseConsolidatedRecord, parseRequestBody)
  • toggle* — flips a single UI state (toggleSessionExpand, toggleMSItem)
  • next* / commit* — the reserve-then-commit pattern used for REF numbers (nextSharedRef/commitSharedRef, nextNoteRef)
  • Noun-first getters (issNames, tsNames, proponentNames, courseByNum) return a derived list or lookup without side effects. If a function only reads and returns, it doesn't need a verb prefix.
Element IDs
Pattern: short lowercase feature prefix (2–5 chars), underscore, descriptive suffix. One prefix per tab or feature, reused consistently across all of that feature's fields. Confirmed prefixes already in use, check here before inventing a new one to avoid an accidental collision:
  • na — Notes Archive / Log Book
  • bg — Budget
  • fa — Funding Request
  • lv — Leave / TDY
  • tr — Training
  • qr — 4713 Review Tool
  • kr — Key Roster
  • tv — Travel
  • tk — Task
  • std — Standards
  • im — IM Reserve (Instructor Meeting)
  • ta — T&A
  • qs — QA Eval Scheduler
  • fnm / fn — File Naming
  • ts — Tasks, the act-on-a-task section
  • pr — Policy Review
  • imp — Console Improvements
  • urlm — URL Manager
  • stinv — STAGE Inventory
  • ss — Session Status Log
  • cm — Course Material
  • ca — Course Assign
  • da — Daily Agenda
  • qae — QA Eval (evaluation records, distinct from qs scheduling)
  • tcfg — Tab Config (Data > Tab Settings: rename/reorder/color for main and child tabs)
  • cm — Course Material (the subbar suite: Timeline, 4713, 4712-1, and the builder shells; uses the same router pattern as Comms, one shared #cmBody)
  • lp — Lesson Plan (ported from the ISS console 2026-07-31; persisted keys use an lp*CM naming pattern, e.g. lpDraftCM, specifically to avoid sharing localStorage with the ISS console's separate copy of this feature)
  • fd — Fixed Dropdowns management (Data > Dropdowns; draft-then-Save editing for STATE.dropdownRegistry, the source of truth for migrated fixed dropdowns elsewhere in the console)
  • pw — Passwords (Comms & Processes; quick lookup tool, private repo only, routine non-sensitive sites)
  • mn — Meeting Notes (Notes tab; turns a captured meeting into real Log Book notes, one per discussion item plus a summary)
  • tpl — Template Editor (Data > Templates; draft-then-Save editing for STATE.templateRegistry, the wording behind migrated generated emails/Memory Hole entries)
These three tokens used to be hardcoded directly in this file's source, visible to anyone who has the file itself. Moved here so they live only in this browser's local storage instead, entered once, never baked into anything that gets shared or copied. Revoke and regenerate all three in GitHub before entering new ones here.
Main Sync Token
Used for courses.json, sessions.json, and every other file in the shared repo (mhefling2-sudo/eddb-console-data). Fine-grained personal access token, Contents read/write scope on that repo only.
Requests Token
Scoped narrowly to GitHub Issues only on the same repo, deliberately cannot touch courses.json or anything else even though it's shared with the ISS console copies.
Notes Token
Used only for the private notes archive repo (mhefling2-sudo/eddb-notes-archive). Never touches the shared/public repo.
Shared Repo Push Token
Used to push any text file (this console, the ISS console, a handoff doc) to the public mhefling2-sudo/eddb-shared repo, so a new Claude session or Code can read it directly instead of a manual upload. Fine-grained personal access token, Contents read/write on that repo only, nothing else.
Consoles on eddb-shared
What version of each console is currently sitting in the repo, read from inside the files themselves rather than from their names, since a downloaded file gets renamed and a name can say anything. Check this before pushing so an older build does not land on top of a newer one.
Not checked yet.
Push File to Repo
For any text file you need available to a new Claude session or to Code without downloading, emailing, and re-uploading: this console, the ISS console, a session handoff doc, anything text-based. Pushes the real file from disk, not this live page's current DOM state (a running single-page app's DOM is not its source file, it's the source plus everything every render function has injected since load). Select the file you actually saved, confirm it's the right one and the destination path looks right, then push. Not for images, PDFs, or other binary files, this reads the file as text.
Destination Path
Pre-filled with a guess based on the filename, always editable. Lands on eddb-shared, main branch.
Commit Message
